title: System Evolution
definition: The process of changing or developing a system over time, often to improve functionality, efficiency, or add new features.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you have a toy car, and you make it better over time. This is like when we change our software to make it better.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: System evolution is the practice of updating, upgrading, or replacing existing software systems to improve functionality, efficiency, or meet new requirements. It can involve restructuring the codebase, adding new features, or removing obsolete components.
difficulty_levels.expert: System evolution is a continuous process that reflects the dynamic nature of software development. It can be seen as a form of adaptation to changing environments, new technologies, and evolving user needs. System evolution involves not only technical aspects but also social and organizational aspects, such as managing the development team, handling legacy code, and dealing with user expectations.

extra_fields.insight: The repository can evolve to include both the full system and the sanitized demo system, allowing new users to learn and explore while providing advanced users with the full functionality.
